label: DF200 arch · 35°

wrist.source: user-confirmed JR DF200 "100° without distortion", 640 × 480 MJPG 4:3, rectilinear -> 87.3° H / 71.1° V (2026-09-15)

params.concept: C3 (forward clamp arch), the concept chosen in the wrist-camera study; DESIGN.md beside this file says why
params.shipped_detent_note: 35° is one of the 7 holes on the index fan the head was printed with (30..60° in 5° steps). It is shipped because the framing model measures from the lens ENTRANCE PUPIL, 8.0 mm in front of the sensor, at which 40° puts the drive servo LED 0.61° INSIDE the frame. Moving the pin is not a reprint: only head.stl and retainer.stl turn about the hinge, and arch.stl and every print/*.stl are untouched.
params.framing_source: gen_wristcam_arch.framing_table() and its landmark table, at hFOV 87.3° (half-vFOV 35.582°)

camera_module.note: The DF200 module and its retainer are part of the SET. `df200.stl` is the volumetric stand-in (36 × 36 × 11 body, Ø20 × 9 barrel, Ø13 × 3 hood, 9 × 5 × 4 connector, sensor 4 mm behind the front face), seated in the pocket with its front face on the 3 mm lip. The connector is on the image-UP axis, so it passes the retainer's 24 × 14 window. The retainer boss presses the module's back face by 0.4 mm - the clamp preload; use a 0.5 mm pocket shim behind a thinner module. Measured on the exported meshes: module ∩ head 0.001 mm³, connector ∩ retainer 0.000 mm³.

connector_corridor.note: kept empty by an unconditional cut in Arch.arch(); the crossbar humps over it

driver_relief.seat_m25: Ø6.4 × 16 mm bored up from each M2.5 counterbore. The legs' inboard faces are at |Y| 19.5, only 0.59 mm outboard of the seat axis, so in rev 1 they roofed all four Ø5.4 counterbores: the head could not be put in and no key could reach it (0.37 mm of clear Ø3.6). It is now 50 mm front / 17 mm rear straight, and 60 mm with a ball-end key.
driver_relief.tool_note: a Ø7 socket never fits an M2.5 head here - the counterbore is Ø5.4. The Ø7 row of the audit records the LeKiwi wrist-roll bracket sitting 1.0 mm over the rear pair, which is inside the stated uncertainty of the PincOpen to wrist-flange registration.

cable_management.tie_lug: a 4 mm tab on the front face of the crown, X -33..-29, |Y| <= 7, Z 57.5..62.5, with a 9 × 2.2 mm slot for a 2.5 mm zip tie
cable_management.servo_lead: Ø5 route: pin headers, up past a 10 mm housing, rearward along the corridor at Z 53.5, out of the arch at X -57. 0.000 mm³ against the arch, the servo, the top plate, the motor flange, the bottom plate and the arm interface. Min bend radius 4.9 mm - the 18.1 mm ceiling over a 10 mm plug is what limits it.
cable_management.df200_pigtail: Ø5 route: retainer window, outboard loop at |Y| 35, down past the -Y cheek, into the corridor, out at X -57. Min bend radius 12.0 mm, 0.54 mm³ (a 0.05 mm brush of the index fan rim). Tie it to a leg - each leg is a free web - and leave a 40 mm service loop for the detent.

bom.seat_front: 2x M2.5 × 10, the FRONT seat pair at X -26.27. Head bears at Z 24.20, so 4.70 mm of stack - a 2.20 mm rise from the seat plane to the pad underside (the flange foot stands 1.86 to 2.18 mm proud of the seat and the remaining 0.02 to 0.34 mm is air) plus the 2.50 mm pad - leaves 5.30 mm in a 6.61 mm blind hole, 1.31 mm spare.
bom.seat_rear: 2x M2.5 × 8, the REAR seat pair at X -41.27. Head bears at Z 22.00, 2.50 mm of stack, 5.50 mm of thread in a 6.61 mm blind hole - 1.11 mm spare. (The rev-1 M2.5 × 8 over a 0.48 mm pad bottomed 0.88 mm before the head touched and never clamped.)
bom.seat_note: Hand torque, no washer needed: the Ø5.4 × 1.5 counterbore leaves 2.50 mm of pad under each head. Bolt the arch on BEFORE the gripper goes back on the wrist - the wrist-roll bracket sits 1.0 mm over the rear pair, and a ball-end key is the only tool that reaches the rear -Y screw with the arm assembled.
bom.hinge: 1x M3 × 60 + nyloc, the head hinge (54.2 mm across both cheeks)
bom.index: 1x M3 × 8, the tilt index pin. The seat in the head is BLIND, 3.0 mm deep: 5.00 cheek + 0.40 gap + 2.60 of seat, and it cannot reach the camera module (0.00 mm³, measured).
bom.retainer_plate: PRINT the shared "Camera retainer plate" upgrade - it is this set's retainer, the same solid to 0.005 mm.
bom.shims: PRINT the shared "Camera pocket shims" upgrade if the module is under 11 mm deep (36 × 36 mm, 0.4 / 0.8 / 1.6 mm).
bom.ties: 2 × 2.5 mm zip tie: one through the crown lug for the servo harness, one round a leg for the DF200 pigtail (leave a 40 mm service loop)

params.pupil_model: margins are measured from the lens ENTRANCE PUPIL, 8.0 mm in front of the sensor point (bracketed at 6 and 10 mm), not from the sensor: the module's own barrel and hood stand 4-16 mm proud of it. At the rev-1 40° detent the servo LED's margin is -0.61° (+1.25 at +6 mm, -2.53 at +10), i.e. the LED is in the frame; at 35° it is +6.66 (+8.50 / +4.78).

access_audit.method: Ø7 × 60 driver cast, Ø3.6 × 60 straight key, and a Ø3.6 cone to 25° for a ball-end key, from each bearing face against the assembled robot at the parked pose; mm of clear tube
access_audit.sequence: take the PincOpen stock camera stack off -> plug the servo lead in -> bolt the arch to the seat (before the gripper goes back on the wrist) -> hang the head on the M3 × 60 hinge -> index pin -> module -> retainer last

shared_plates.retainer: The shared "Camera retainer plate" print-only upgrade - the same solid as this set's own retainer mesh to 0.005 mm (measured on the exported meshes). Printed once, it serves every camera head this project builds: the corner mast and the wrist arch.
shared_plates.pocket_shims: The shared "Camera pocket shims" print-only upgrade - 36 × 36 mm at 0.4 / 0.8 / 1.6 mm, with the same 24 × 14 window. Stack them for 0.4 to 2.8 mm in 0.4 mm steps.

tilt_index.hinge: M3 × 60 through both cheeks (54.2 mm of stack)
tilt_index.pin: M3 × 8 into a BLIND 3.0 mm seat

framing_gates.note: the drive servo LED and the servo's forward-top corner out of frame with at least 4.7° of margin at EVERY pupil offset in the bracket, the grasp point inside the frame, and both pads inside it closed and at 40 mm open

params.gates_note: Gates: the servo LED and the servo nose out of frame by at least 4.7° at every pupil offset in the bracket, |v_grasp| <= 1, and both pads in frame closed and at 40 mm open. At hFOV 87.3° only 30° and 35° pass, by 9.25 and 1.96° of LED margin over the gate. The rest fail the LED gate: 40° by 5.31°, 45° by 12.56°, 50° by 19.79°, 55° by 26.99°, 60° by 34.16°. 35° is shipped as the steeper of the two that pass, so it keeps the most gripper-relative resolution.

notes:
DF200 arch · 35°. Sensor (-19.9583, 0.0000, 99.2316) at the shipped 35° detent, optical axis (0.819152, 0.000000, -0.573576); hFOV 87.3 / vFOV 71.1 (JR DF200). 2 plates, 42.0 g of PLA, tallest 88.3 mm in Z: `arch` 49.3 × 54.2 × 88.3 mm, 25.0 g; `head` 43.4 × 68.5 × 17.5 mm, 17.0 g. Robot-frame meshes drawn by the studio: arch.stl, df200.stl, head.stl, retainer.stl.

The plate count is down to the parts that carry load: the list above IS the set. The retainer plate and the pocket shims are the two SHARED print-only upgrades, "Camera retainer plate" and "Camera pocket shims", which this set references instead of shipping a second copy. The retainer is the same solid as this set's own retainer mesh to 0.005 mm, measured on the exported meshes. The tilt index seat in the head is BLIND at 3.0 mm and its pin is M3 × 8, so the pin cannot enter the camera module, and the head's cable duct is vertical and inside the wall.

This is the WRIST mount: a two-plate forward clamp arch on the PincOpen camera face, carrying the same head, retainer and module as the corner mast. The legs are TRUE 4 mm plates (rev 1's measured 0.54-0.84 mm perpendicular); the front pads sit ON the Motor_Flange feet instead of 1.1 mm above them; the seat screws are sized to the measured stacks; and it prints UPRIGHT, 398.5 mm² of flat bed contact against 0.0 in rev 1. The crossbar HUMPS over the STS3215 connector band (Z 57.5..62.5 over |Y| <= 13) so the servo can still be plugged in with the arch on - 18.1 mm of clear air over the socket face, and the corridor stays open to the rear - and a zip-tie lug on the crown anchors the harness. The shipped detent is 35° rather than the design 40 because the framing model measures from the lens ENTRANCE PUPIL, 8.0 mm in front of the sensor. At 40° the drive servo's LED is 0.61° INSIDE the frame; at 35° it clears by 6.66°. The `pupil_model` and `framing` blocks of this file carry that table.

Hardware beyond the printed plates - the 9 lines of `params.bom`, which the generator builds for THIS variant: `seat_front`, `seat_rear`, `seat_note`, `hinge`, `index`, `retainer`, `retainer_plate`, `shims`, `ties`.

Design tilt 45°, shipped detent 35°. The index fan was printed with 7 holes (30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55, 60°) and the head and the retainer are those same meshes rotated about the hinge, so moving the index pin is NOT a reprint and every `print/*.stl` is unchanged by it - `params.shipped_detent_note` records why the shipped hole moved. `df200.stl` is the camera-module stand-in (36 × 36 × 11 body, Ø20 × 9 barrel, Ø13 × 3 hood, 9 × 5 × 4 connector, sensor 4 mm behind the front face) seated in the head pocket at that detent with its front face on the 3 mm lip, connector along the image-UP axis so it passes the retainer's 24 × 14 window. Measured on the meshes this run exported: module ∩ head 0.000 mm³, module ∩ retainer 206.000 mm³, connector ∩ retainer 0.000 mm³.

Assembly order, the fastener-by-fastener driver-access cast and the cable routes are in `ASSEMBLY.md` beside this file; `DESIGN.md` is the design record and the alternatives this one was chosen against. Every measured number behind them is in this set's own `params` block.
summary: Research concept C3: a gusseted forward arch off the PincOpen camera seat (Z 19.50, 4x M2.5 at X -41.27/-26.27, Y ±18.91) that STRADDLES the STS3215 drive servo and carries the same insertable 36.4 × 36.4 clamp pocket, module and retainer the corner mast uses. TWO printed plates - arch, head. Sensor (-19.96, 0, 99.23) PincOpen mm, 35° below the finger direction, DF200 hFOV 87.3 / vFOV 71.1.

hinge.positive: a right-hand turn about the axis raises the tilt
